screening_reasoning: Validates LLM-ensemble abstract screening across 23 Cochrane systematic reviews with large-scale quantitative evaluation (n=119,695), demonstrating workload reductions of 37-99% while maintaining sensitivity. Directly addresses LLM-based screening pipeline evaluation with benchmark metrics.

Presents EligMeta, an agentic framework integrating automated trial discovery with eligibility-aware meta-analysis using a hybrid LLM-deterministic architecture. Provides quantitative evaluation on gastric cancer and olaparib datasets demonstrating reproducible evidence synthesis.

Proposes AutoConfidenceScore, an LLM-driven framework for predicting preprint publication to support systematic review inclusion decisions. Reports AUROC of 0.747 with automated NLP extraction and semantic embeddings, reducing manual curation burden.

Evaluates six LLMs for full-text methodological assessment of mediation analysis studies against expert consensus, achieving near-human accuracy (F1 correlation 0.95). Provides a reproducible framework for criterion-specific human-AI collaboration in evidence synthesis.

Introduces a framework evaluating LLM hallucination rates in reference generation and factual consistency of review composition, with publicly available code and dataset. Addresses reference hallucination mitigation for literature reviews but does not propose a system/harness (no INC-01).

Presents BioResearcher, a scenario-guided multi-agent system with 30+ tools for translational medicine evidence synthesis, featuring claim-level multi-model reconciliation and provenance preservation. Evaluated on 109 unit tests, BixBench, and a 30-query clinical benchmark.

Introduces MedMeta benchmark evaluating LLM ability to synthesize meta-analysis conclusions from medical abstracts, comparing Golden-RAG against parametric-only workflows. Demonstrates that RAG grounding is critical and identifies vulnerabilities in evidence synthesis.

Presents BioInsight, a provenance-preserving multi-agent orchestration framework with typed artifact contracts and decoupled evidence acquisition for biomedical knowledge discovery. Evaluates on standardized QA and evidence synthesis tasks, demonstrating improved traceability over baselines.

Practitioner experience report using LLMs throughout a systematic mapping study, documenting both efficiency gains (time reduction, standardization) and challenges (prompt engineering effort, hallucinations). Provides practical recommendations though lacks quantitative system evaluation.

Proposes PRISMA-DFLLM, an extended reporting-guidelines framework combining PRISMA with domain-specific finetuned LLMs for systematic reviews. Introduces a checklist and technical roadmap but presents no empirical evaluation or computational artifact (no INC-04).

Presents ARIS, an open-source research harness with cross-model adversarial collaboration, 65+ reusable skills, and a three-stage claim assurance layer (integrity verification, result-to-claim mapping, claim auditing). Directly addresses provenance, hallucination mitigation, and autonomous research orchestration.

MEDSYN benchmarks multimodal LLMs on clinical evidence synthesis for differential diagnosis, targeting clinical decision-making rather than scholarly literature review workflows. Clinical domain does not match the academic literature harness focus.

AdaMem proposes an adaptive memory framework for long-horizon dialogue agents, targeting general conversational AI rather than scholarly literature research. General agent/dialogue memory is outside the academic evidence-synthesis domain.

Educational experience report describing how software engineering students used LLMs in a course assignment, based on student disclosure statements. No computational artifact or system is proposed; purely a pedagogical reflection.

Presents AutoSynthesis, an end-to-end multi-agent system automating the full meta-analysis pipeline from search strategy formulation through PRISMA-aligned report generation. Achieves pooled effect estimates close to expert-conducted meta-analyses, with heterogeneity analysis and risk-of-bias assessment.

Semi-structured interview study with 44 novice researchers on privacy perceptions in LLM-assisted workflows, with no computational system or artifact proposed. The qualitative findings address privacy concerns but not a research harness.

Preregistered comparison of human versus LLM screening workflows in a conceptually complex scoping review, evaluating recall-workload trade-offs and run-to-run consistency across multiple models and configurations. Provides operational evidence on LLM screening deployment properties.

Presents an AI co-scientist platform for PICOS-based knowledge synthesis integrating vector retrieval and a Neo4j knowledge graph, with quantitative evaluation including 95.7% study-design classification accuracy and demonstrated RAG advantages for structured queries.

GRACE-RAG proposes a governed graph-augmented retrieval architecture for institutional question answering, showing quality gains of up to 20%. However, it targets closed-domain institutional settings rather than scholarly literature research harnesses (no INC-01).

Presents Brain Researcher, an agentic research harness for neuroimaging with claim-scoping rules, multiverse analysis, and provenance-linked decision audit. Demonstrates 70.2pp improvement in tool-selection accuracy and scientific review classification of claim status.
